'''John Coleman Moore''' (May 27, 1923 – January 1, 2016) was an American mathematician. The [[Borel−Moore homology]] and [[Eilenberg–Moore spectral sequence]] are named after him.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rusin|first=Dave|url=http://www.math.niu.edu/~rusin/known-math/98/MSC.names|title=People whose names are embedded in Math Subject Classification|year=1998|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130604060909/http://www.math.niu.edu/%7Erusin/known-math/98/MSC.names|archive-date=2013-06-04}}. Updated February 2005.</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Moore was born in 1923 in [[Staten Island]], [[New York (state)|New York]].<ref>Pamela Kalte et al. ''American Men and Women of Science'', 22. Edition, Thomson Gale 2005</ref> He received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in 1948 from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and his [[Ph.D.]] in 1952 from [[Brown University]] under the supervision of [[George W. Whitehead]].

== Career ==
Moore began his career at [[Princeton University]] as an instructor, and was eventually promoted to full professor in 1961. He retired from Princeton in 1989, after which he took a half-time position at the [[University of Rochester]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.princeton.edu/news/department-remembers-john-coleman-moore-1923-2016|title=Department Remembers John Coleman Moore (1925-2016)| year=2018|publisher=Princeton University, Department of Mathematics}}</ref>

His most-cited paper is on [[Hopf algebra]]s, co-authored with [[John Milnor]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Milnor | first1 = John W. |author1-link=John Milnor| last2 = Moore | first2 = John C. | title = On the structure of Hopf algebras | journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]] | volume = 81 | issue = 2 | year = 1965 | pages = 211–264 | doi = 10.2307/1970615 | jstor=1970615| url = https://polipapers.upv.es/index.php/AGT/article/view/2250 }}.</ref> As a faculty member at [[Princeton University]], he advised 24 students and is the [[academic genealogy|academic ancestor]] of over 1000 mathematicians.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=4350}}</ref> He was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1958<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=Princeton Alumni Weekly|title=7 Princetonians at the International Congress of Mathematicians|date=9 May 1958|pages=14|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UxJbAAAAYAAJ&pg=RA8-PA66}}</ref> in [[Edinburgh]] and in 1970 in [[Nice]].

In 1983, a conference on [[K-theory]] was held at Princeton in honor of Moore's 60th birthday.<ref>{{cite book | last = Browder | first = William | authorlink=William Browder (mathematician) | title = Algebraic Topology and Algebraic K-Theory: Proceedings of a Conference, October 24-28, 1983 at Princeton University, Dedicated to John C. Moore on His 60th Birthday | publisher = [[Princeton University Press]] | year = 1987 | isbn = 0-691-08426-2}}.</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title= List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|access-date= 2013-02-10}}</ref> He died in 2016 at the age of 92.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.princeton.edu/main/news/archive/S46/01/33E45/index.xml?section=topstories|title=John C. Moore, dedicated and influential Princeton mathematician, dies|first=Morgan|last=Kelly|date=2016|publisher=Princeton University}}.</ref>
